sections.html:
Lawrence sits on the northeast side of Indianapolis, in Lawrence Township, Marion County, about 9 miles from downtown. The 2020 count was 49,370 residents in 19,067 households, up steadily from 38,915 in 2000. That growth left a mix of housing ages, from older homes near the original town center to newer subdivisions farther out.

Lawrence is one of four excluded cities under Unigov, the 1969 merger of Indianapolis and Marion County, so it kept its own municipal government. City rules on code compliance and permits come from Lawrence, while county services such as the property tax bill and recording come from Marion County.

sections.h2: Fort Harrison and the northeast edge
sections.html:
Fort Benjamin Harrison operated as a U.S. Army post from 1906 until 1991. The site has since been redeveloped with residential neighborhoods, a golf course and Fort Harrison State Park, which covers 1,700 acres with trails, a nature center and fishing access to Fall Creek. The Fort Benjamin Harrison Historic District, listed on the National Register in 1995, covers about 360 acres and includes 100 contributing buildings.

If your house sits near the historic district, ask the city whether any local review applies before you plan exterior work.

Lawrence has hot, humid summers and mild to cold winters, with about 46.6 inches of precipitation a year. June is the wettest month at 5.96 inches. Wet springs and summers test basements, sump pumps, gutters and grading.

Fall Creek runs through the northwest part of the city. If your lot is close to it, look up the flood zone before you list, since insurers and lenders check it.

Housing in Lawrence ranges from older homes near the original town center to newer subdivisions farther out, and the work a buyer expects follows the age. An older house may need wiring, plumbing, roof or foundation work. A newer one may need little beyond cosmetic updates and a worn roof or furnace.

Neither kind is hard to sell as-is. The point is to know what you have before you talk to buyers, so the price you are offered reflects the house and not a guess.

Violations can be reported through a link on the city website.

The Division of Code Compliance enforces municipal code in Lawrence. Its work covers minimum property maintenance standards, building codes, permitting requirements and licensing, and it works toward voluntary compliance.

If you own a vacant or neglected house, a notice from this office is a common starting point for a sale. An as-is buyer takes over the repairs and the compliance conversation, so you do not have to clear the notice first. Call the office to find out what is open on your address.

sections.h2: Fix it first or sell as-is?
sections.html:
Go through the house the way a buyer's inspector would, noting the roof, furnace, water heater, basement, plumbing and electrical. Get rough quotes and add the weeks the work will take. A buyer with a mortgage usually responds to an inspection with a repair request or a lower offer, and the lender may insist on fixes before closing. A cash buyer prices the condition from the start.

If the work would use up most of what it adds to the price, or you cannot front the money, selling as-is can leave you with about the same net and much less effort.

Lawrence is in Marion County, so the Marion County Recorder files the deed once the sales disclosure form is done. Indiana Code 6-1.1-5.5-3 has the parties complete the form, the county assessor approve it and the auditor process any deduction.

Property tax comes due on May 10 and November 10. Your closing agent will tell you how the current installment is divided with the buyer, and your tax bill shows which installments are paid. For exact dates and any weekend adjustment, phone the Marion County treasurer. Tax owed at closing is paid from your proceeds.

U.S. 36, Pendleton Pike, runs through Lawrence. Interstate 465, the Indianapolis beltway, meets U.S. 36 at Exit 42 in the southwest corner, and Exit 40 at East 56th Street and North Shadeland Avenue lies along the western border. The beltway puts the rest of the Indianapolis metro within a drive.

The Metropolitan School District of Lawrence Township runs public K-12 education, with Lawrence Central and Lawrence North high schools. The district office is at 6501 Sunnyside Rd. Confirm the district for your exact address before you describe the house.

sections.h2: What Lawrence sellers usually deal with
sections.html:
Lawrence owners tend to sell after inheriting a house, wearing out on a rental, facing a repair backlog or taking a job elsewhere. Listings here compete with homes across Marion County and the surrounding counties.

  • Traditional listing: prep, showings and a buyer who has to clear financing and inspection.
  • For sale by owner: saves the commission but adds paperwork and marketing.
  • Cash sale: skips repairs and lets you choose the closing date.

Set net proceeds side by side for all three before you choose.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
1. Send the address and describe the house, any tenants and any code notice.
  2. We look at the property and make an offer.
  3. If you accept, the title company opens the file and searches the deed for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign the deed paperwork and the sales disclosure form.
  5. The Marion County Recorder files the deed, and you receive your proceeds.

Most delays come from the title search: an old lien, a deed that still shows a former owner or estate papers still outstanding. Mention those on the first call.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
We buy Lawrence houses as-is. You tell us about the house, we make an offer, and if you accept, a title company searches the deed, prepares the disclosure form and sets a closing date. Repairs and cleaning stay with the buyer.

Bring your tax bill, any lease and payoff figures to the first call, and ask for the closing date in writing.

This route is not right for every owner. Compare it with a listing, counting the repair bills, the showings and the monthly cost of holding a house that has not sold.

An inherited Lawrence house may need probate before a deed can be prepared, and it may need a clean-out. Heirs who live elsewhere often pay utilities, insurance and tax on a house nobody uses, and a neglected one can draw a code notice. Gather the estate papers, the tax bill and the keys, and ask the title company what the deed needs.

A rental sold with a tenant keeps its lease. Collect the lease and tell any buyer the rent, deposit and term.

faqs.q: Is Lawrence, Indiana part of Indianapolis?
faqs.a: Lawrence is in Marion County and borders Indianapolis, but it is an excluded city under Unigov and keeps its own government. Residents still vote in Indianapolis city elections.

faqs.q: Who handles code violations in Lawrence?
faqs.a: The Division of Code Compliance in the Department of Public Works. It is at 9001 East 59th Street, and the phone is (317) 545-6191.
The Metropolitan School District of Lawrence Township, with Lawrence Central and Lawrence North high schools. Confirm the district for your exact address.

faqs.q: When are Indiana property taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments are due May 10 and November 10. Marion County's treasurer can confirm the exact dates and any weekend adjustment.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Lawrence house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so repairs and cleaning stay with the buyer.
